rv.q: Theatre in the Dark's 90-minute version, adapted and directed by Corey Bradberry , moves with the kind of relentless focus that Captain Ahab himself brings to his monomaniacal obsession with vengeance against the white whale that took his leg and his last vestige of reason.
Brilliantly adapted from the novel by Herman Melville, “Moby Dick in the Dark” is a treat for fans of old-time radio.

However, even with all the excess whale fat trimmed away, Moby Dick in the Dark still struggled to hold my attention over its short runtime – and despite the care woven into its storytelling, I simply didn’t connect with it.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this Zoom radio-play adaptation of Melville's classic. The iambic pentameter script and audio-only format earn praise from some, while others find the execution uneven. Scores range widely from 57 to 89.
